office_does: A Port of Bellingham commissioner sits on the newly expanded five-member board that sets policy for the county-wide port's shipping terminal, airport, marinas and waterfront property; all Whatcom County voters elect the District 4 seat in November.
race_blurb: This is one of two new seats created when voters expanded the commission in 2025. Whichever new commissioner draws more votes gets a three-year term and the other a one-year term, though VoteWA lists both as one year. Lynden fisherman and seafood-trucking owner Paul Burrill, the port's marina advisory chair since 2018, faces Bellingham financial planner and ship-logistics coordinator Tor Benson.

candidates.summary: Lynden commercial fisherman of 30-plus years, seafood-company shareholder and trucking-company owner who has chaired the port's marina advisory committee since 2018; first-time candidate.
highlights: Placed first of six in the primary with 30.2% in late returns [S8]
Wants some waterfront land kept permanently industrial and growth built on seafood, cold storage and logistics [S5]
Proposes a heavy-industry advisory committee and more port work for local contractors [S5][S6]
Endorsed by Commissioner Bobby Briscoe, two former commissioners, the Realtors and Firefighters Local 106 [S3]

candidates.summary: Bellingham Certified Financial Planner and former Alaska fishing-boat skipper who coordinates cargo and tanker port calls; first-time candidate in Whatcom with past planning-board service in Petersburg, Alaska.
highlights: Placed second of six in the primary with 24.2% in late returns [S10]
Says the airport and shipping terminal are budgeted at a loss for a third year; backs a 5% airport marketing budget [S1][S5]
Calls for better public communication after ABC Recycling and a review of port-owned property [S2][S5]
Endorsed by the Whatcom Commercial Fishermen's Association and the Nooksack Indian Tribe [S8]
